title: Katy Jewett Organizer Boot Camp
description:
The Organizer Bootcamp is a day-long training designed to provide participants with the skills needed to organize for power. Participants will map their community, make a plan for reaching people who need help after a disaster, and canvass to learn how to have effective organizing conversations. 

We don’t believe in practice without purpose - this training is a dry run for the disasters we know are coming; participants will be on call if a storm strikes this summer to help mobilize aid in the community. 

Participants in the bootcamp are eligible to apply to be a Katy Jewett Organizer Apprentice in fall 2025. This is a fully paid 16-month program that starts with four months of on-the-job, full-time, fully-paid organizing training, and continues with a 12-month job at a local organization doing outreach work in the community.

Learn more: katyjewett.org

President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

title: Reclaim Idaho 2025 Summer Update Zoom - Tues (6/17)
description:
Please join us for a statewide update zoom to get an update on the fight against voucher expansion. On June 17th, we’ll be meeting at 6:30pm MT / 5:30pm PT to discuss the crisis of private school vouchers in Idaho and what we're doing about it.
 
During the 2025 legislative session, Idaho lawmakers passed House Bill 93 and enacted a $50 million school-voucher program. For the first time in state history, Idaho tax dollars will be used to subsidize the cost of tuition for private-school families. 

The special-interest groups promoting vouchers have made clear that the $50 million program is only the beginning. During next year’s legislative session, they intend to remove the $50-million cap and expand the program to all private-school families, including the wealthy, at an estimated cost of $339 million per year.
 
Such a massive expansion of vouchers would bankrupt Idaho and drain millions from public schools. For the benefit of a small number of private-school families, it would defund the public education system that serves 94% of Idaho’s kids. 

It may be inevitable that the legislature tries to expand House Bill 93, but it is not inevitable that they will succeed. To stop this attack on public schools, we need to get organized. Please sign up if you can make it and we hope to see you soon!

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. "12 Days to Democracy", a grassroots group founded by Judy Shatkin, MD,  will begin its significant multi-day march and celebration of justice, community, and love, in the City of Brotherly Love on Monday, June 16, 2025. 

We will journey from Philadelphia's Dilworth Park (at City Hall) to Washington, D.C., from June 16 to June 28, 2025. 

Join us in solidarity to celebrate our freedoms with many community events planned for each stop. 

Come for the trek, the day, or an hour. Can't march? There are lots of opportunities to help and support us.

Check it out at https://www.democracy12.com/.

Register at https://bit.ly/MarchD12. Click "Continue to destination" at the bottom and proceed.
accessibility_notes:
ROADWAYS
We are avoiding high-speed roadways.  The majority of the march is on sidewalks, and when there is no sidewalk, we have three cars to flank the walkers. 
We have an RV traveling with us, equipped with a shower and a toilet.

NOTE: There will be water breaks every 45-60 minutes during the march. We encourage participants to bring their favorite electrolyte tablet, and we will have plenty of water available to participants at all times.

description:
Join us to canvass in the Milton area with Debra Shigley for State Senate! GA Senate District 21 runs through Cherokee and Fulton Counties and the seat is vacant, meaning we have the opportunity to elect a Democrat to office this summer. title: Wayne County Town Hall
description:
Our three representatives, Sens. Fetterman and McCormick and Congressman Bresnahan have been invited. If our representatives do not RSVP, the event becomes an empty chair town hall. As constituents, we deserve to have our questions answered. The town hall will be filmed and sent to each respective legislator. Join us in showing them the voices of Wayne County.

The town hall will focus on the impact of the Budget Reconciliation Bill now in the Senate and its potential impacts on Wayne County resident. Please bring your questions and come to learn more about what is in this 1,100 page bill. The Budget Reconciliation Bill will affect life here in Wayne County and we deserve a say in our future. Come willing to share your stories on how this bill will affect you, or how federal funding already has. Together, we can make our voices heard.

title: Join Indivisible Groups Marching In July 5 Hudson Booster Days Parade
description:
We invite you and yours to march with Hudson WI area Indivisible groups in the Hudson WI Booster Days Parade on Saturday, July 5, with lineup at 10AM and the parade start at 11AM! 

Our Hudson WI area Indivisible groups have Indivisible banners, US flags, signs affirming progressive American values and policies, candy to hand out, tambourines, cowbells, and a snare drum all ready to go. 

Now we need you, your family, and your friends, too! Join us in marching, carrying signs and flags, and smiling and waving in support of our Constitution and our democracy!

Please march with us! We are the people protecting and preserving our US Constitution and our democracy from daily attacks being made upon it by the current president's administration. 

You’re welcome to bring your own flags and signs affirming progressive American values and policies, but please DO NOT make any mention by name of the man currently in the White House.

Please share this info and invite others to join us, too! Indivisible is our neighbors and friends working together for our American progressive values. Indivisible is constituent power working to protect, preserve, and make our American democracy stronger.

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON:
description:
Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of nonviolent action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

On July 17, the anniversary of Congressman John Lewis’s passing, we’re taking action across the country to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of Good Trouble.

From voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act to the criminalization of protest, the Trump administration is launching a full-scale attack on our civil and human rights. But we know the truth: in America, the power lies with the people, and we’re rising to prove it.

This is more than a protest; it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** A core principle behind our Good Trouble Lives On actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.
